title: Finance Assistant
description:
- Finance Assistant
- 2-3 Month Temp, chance to go permanent
- £30-35k, hybrid, immediate start

Finance Assistant
Do you want a job where the ledger actually balances by the time you go home? We're looking for a Finance Assistant to cover a busy period, initially for 2-3 months, full time, hybrid, with a genuine chance of the role going permanent for the right person. You'll take real ownership of the transactional side of the finance function, invoices, credit cards and sales ledger, working alongside budget holders and the wider finance team.
This one suits someone who already knows their way around a busy finance desk and wants to get stuck in from week one. You'll need to be quick with numbers, comfortable picking up new systems, and genuinely careful with the detail, because a lot of what lands on this desk needs to be right first time, not fixed later.

What You Will Be Doing
- Processing purchase orders, invoices, petty cash and credit card transactions day to day, keeping everything moving at pace.
- Checking every entry has proper authorisation before it goes anywhere near the finance system.
- Managing supplier relationships, sorting out queries as they come up and keeping payments running to terms.
- Helping put together the weekly payment run, with everything checked and authorised at each stage.
- Working through company credit card statements line by line, matching every transaction to what's been posted.
- Chasing overdue accounts through calls and standard letters, and flagging the ones that need pushing further up.
- Handling internal recharges between departments accurately and on schedule.
- Getting the bank reconciliation done on time, coding everything correctly as you go.
- Carrying out due diligence on any new supplier, including independently verifying bank details before that first payment is made.
- Being a point of contact for more junior colleagues, showing them the ropes on purchasing processes.

What We Need From You
- Available immediately or on a short notice period, this cover is needed straight away.
- A genuinely careful approach, this role handles a high volume of transactions and mistakes aren't easily hidden.
- Experience in a fast-moving office where you're used to juggling priorities.
- A finance background with hands-on purchase ledger, sales ledger or similar transactional experience.
- Comfortable learning a new finance system quickly if ours isn't one you've used.
- Able to work independently but just as happy mucking in as part of a team.
- Confident communicating with people at every level of the business, not just within finance.
- AAT or equivalent hands-on experience.
- Willing to undergo an enhanced DBS check, this is required for the role.

What's in it for you
- A real shot at a permanent role if you're the right fit, this isn't cover for the sake of it.
- Hybrid working.
- Exposure to a growing, varied organisation.
- No two days looking quite the same.
- Proper support and training while you find your feet.
- A team that will genuinely have your back.
- On-site parking.

If you're someone who takes pride in getting the numbers right, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Mental Health Act Administrator
description: Are you an experienced Mental Health Act Administrator with a passion for ensuring legal compliance and supporting excellent patient care? Elizabeth House is looking for a dedicated and organised Mental Health Act (MHA) Administrator to join our multidisciplinary team. This is an exciting opportunity to play a vital role in ensuring that all Mental Health Act processes are managed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with statutory requirements. As our MHA Administrator, you will work closely with the Hospital Director, Responsible Clinicians, nursing teams, and external agencies to ensure the hospital maintains the highest standards of legal compliance and governance. You will be responsible for the administration of all aspects of the Mental Health Act 1983 (as amended), ensuring legal documentation is accurate, compliant, and processed within statutory timescales. You will provide expert advice to staff, coordinate Mental Health Tribunal and Hospital Managers' Hearings, maintain legal records, and support the organisation during CQC inspections and internal audits. Key Responsibilities Administer all Mental Health Act documentation in line with current legislation and the Mental Health Act Code of Practice. Scrutinise detention papers for legal accuracy and identify any anomalies. Maintain the Mental Health Act Tracker and monitor statutory deadlines, renewals, consent to treatment requirements, and appeals. Coordinate Mental Health Tribunals and Hospital Managers' Hearings. Liaise with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), Tribunal Service, Responsible Clinicians, Independent Hospital Managers, IMHAs, and other stakeholders. Ensure statutory rights are explained and appropriate documentation is provided to patients. Maintain secure legal files and ensure clinical records are updated appropriately. Complete monthly audits of Mental Health Act documentation and legal files. Produce governance reports and compliance data. Provide advice and guidance to staff on Mental Health Act processes. Support the delivery of Mental Health Act training across the service.
